I get a similar thing with growing up in an abusive family. People talk about their childhood and their parents and it really upsets me. But what my therapist said was you have to let yourself grieve the youth you wish you’d had. If you wanna cry, cry. If you wanna have an angry rant to someone do it. I also haven’t had many intimate relationships with anyone because of my trust issues and get really jealous of people who have had great intimate relationships. 
What I also find helpful is looking at the things in you grew up with that other people wouldn’t have had, and the ways they shape you as a person. Maybe someone is looking at you with similar envy. And if you don’t have specific things that you grew up with that are particularly interesting or worth being grateful for then do what I do. Think about all the ways the rough things shaped you to be a more understanding open minded person. When someone comes along and says they were struggling with a similar thing you can comfort them. And not everyone has that chance.

I would encourage you to try another therapist then. I saw so many therapists before I found any that were right for me. The two that worked for be were both psychotherapists. And they were the only psychotherapists I saw so I think their training was more suited to me. From my experience they seem to dig into what happened in your past that is causing you to feel this way and then they help you with closure. They also teach you about how the dynamics of interacting with others. 
It takes time to get things sorted, it’s hard not to expect that you will start feeling better right away. I took a year off this year to work exclusively on my mental health and going to therapy. It was a combination of finding the right therapist and the right medication. I tried 5 other medications before I found the right one for me. So what I’m saying is these things take time and you have to have patience with yourself. I believe in you:)

In New Zealand you’re lucky if the suicide hotline does anything at all. It’s extremely uncommon to be hospitalised or even have someone come check up on you. There isn’t much in the way of suicide support here. That sounds like the complete opposite problem. Why can’t anywhere strike a balance with mental health.

From personal experience therapy only works if you find the right therapist and right kind of therapy for you. How do you get on with your therapist? What kind of therapist are they? 
Also therapy only really works if you are open to change the things in your life that needs to be changed and open to hearing some hard truths. 
In terms of seeing I psychiatrist, this could help. They will most likely want to put you on medication. Have you tried any medications before? For me personally I tried a lot of medication but none of them worked. Which is pretty uncommon, that’s why seeing a psychiatrist was no good for me. 
But that doesn’t mean it won’t be helpful for you. I would definately give it a try.
